title: Q4 v3: orchestrator/planner_router.py — Planner tier router: modes off|shadow|active, hard vs soft Fable escalation, evidence gate, Fable reserve, hold instead of silent downgrade; decision_log kind planner_route (P5, P9, P11, P17, P18)
spec:
Why: decision.route (orchestrator/decision.py) decides routine/investigate/escalate and names escalate_tier fable; planner_runs.launch_routed (lines 1090-1110) resolves that alias to [models].planner. There is no Opus tier between investigate (sonnet) and escalate (fable), no hard/soft split, no evidence gate, no Fable reserve and no hold path (brief P5, P9, P11, P17, P18). Spec reviews T-0681 and of T-0692 are folded in (plain notify with a module-level warned set, record() inputs, dict access, classification producer, extra as a dict, numeric band fallback, candidates content, reasons in the hard branch, reserve helper, jev_mode ownership).
What: new pure module orchestrator/planner_router.py plus one new entry "planner_route" in decision_log.KINDS. No bus, pool or file reads; inputs never mutated. Every structured input is a plain dict read with .get(): ctx (decision.route's ctx dict, see decision.py docstring; callers add ctx["complexity"] = task complexity for held, goal complexity otherwise), classification (planner_taxonomy.classify output from orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py on goal/T-0674: keys decision_type, architectural, ambiguous, risk_class none|low|high, signals, band, task_class), evidence ({"n": int, "noninferior": True|False|None, "reescalation_rate": float}; produced later by planner_scorecard.class_evidence in this goal; consumed only), availability ({tier: {"available": bool, "reason": str}, "fable_reserve_ok": bool}), jev_signal ({"soft_adjust": float} or None). route is decision.Route (attributes name, reason, evidence, tier) or a dict with those keys; a tiny _get(obj, key, default) helper reads both.
- load_cfg(pool_cfg) -> dict: the ONE reader of pool.toml [planner.routing] for every module in this goal. Keys and defaults: mode "shadow" (off|shadow|active), default_tier "opus", escalation_tier "fable", hard_complexity_min 9, hard_security True, hard_spec_review_request_changes_min 2, hard_ambiguous True, min_samples 20, shadow_sample_rate 1.0, fable_reserve_share 0.2, jev_mode "shadow" (off|shadow|active; read by jev_planner through this dict), soft_threshold 0.5. Module docstring carries a table key -> consumer (mode/default_tier/escalation_tier/hard_*/min_samples/soft_threshold: this module; shadow_sample_rate: this module and planner_shadow.eligible; fable_reserve_share: fable_reserve_ok below, called by planner_runs when it builds availability; jev_mode: jev_planner). An invalid mode or jev_mode, or a non-numeric number, -> default plus one plain notify.notify(f"pool.toml [planner.routing].{key} invalid ({value!r}); using {default!r}") per key per process via a module-level set _WARNED; never raises, never touches the bus.
- fable_reserve_ok(headroom_share, cfg) -> bool: headroom_share None -> True (unlimited budget); else headroom_share >= cfg["fable_reserve_share"].
- BAND_FLOOR = {"1-3": 1, "4-6": 4, "7-10": 7}; effective_complexity(classification, ctx) -> int: ctx["complexity"] when it is an int, else BAND_FLOOR.get(classification band, 0). With the default hard_complexity_min 9 a missing ctx complexity can never hard-escalate on band alone (floor 7).
- @dataclass(frozen=True) RouterDecision: tier (str), mode (str), hard (bool), hold (bool), hold_reason (str|None), reasons (tuple[str, ...]), hard_reasons (tuple[str, ...]), soft_score (float), shadow_tier (str|None), candidates (tuple[str, ...]) = (default_tier, escalation_tier) always, evidence (dict), decision_type (str).
- hard_escalation(classification, ctx, route, cfg) -> list[str]: route name != "escalate" -> []; route reason startswith "unknown:" or == "routes_disabled" -> "unknown_risk"; effective_complexity >= hard_complexity_min -> "complexity"; hard_security and (risk_class == "high" or ctx security_trigger or touches_auth or touches_data_deletion) -> "security"; hard_ambiguous and decision_type in ("architectural_replan", "ambiguous_requirement") -> "architectural_or_ambiguous"; ctx spec_review_request_changes >= hard_spec_review_request_changes_min -> "repeated_spec_rejection"; auto_fix_rounds_used and auto_fix_rounds both ints and used >= cap -> "lineage_cap"; ctx reescalation truthy -> "reescalation".
- soft_score(classification, ctx, evidence, jev_signal=None) -> float in [0, 1]: +0.3 architectural; +0.2 effective_complexity in (7, 8); +0.2 evidence reescalation_rate > 0.2; +0.2 evidence noninferior is False; +0.1 risk_class low; plus jev soft_adjust clamped to [-0.2, 0.2]; clamp to [0, 1]. Tokens/usd never inputs (docstring).
- decide(classification, ctx, route, *, cfg, availability, evidence, jev_signal=None, sample=1.0) -> RouterDecision, rules in order: route name != "escalate" -> tier = route tier or "fable", reasons ("not_escalate_route",), hard False, unchanged in every mode. mode off -> tier route tier or "fable", reasons ("mode_off",), shadow_tier None. hard_reasons non-empty -> hard True, tier escalation_tier, reasons = hard_reasons; escalation tier unavailable -> hold True, hold_reason f"fable_unavailable:{reason}", reasons = hard_reasons + ("hold",) (never downgrade, jev ignored). mode shadow -> tier escalation_tier, reasons ("shadow_production_fable",); shadow_tier default_tier when default tier available and sample <= shadow_sample_rate, else None with reason shadow_default_unavailable or sampled_out appended. mode active, not hard: default_tier when evidence noninferior is True and n >= min_samples and soft_score < soft_threshold ("evidence_noninferior"); elif availability fable_reserve_ok is False and noninferior is not False -> default_tier ("fable_reserve_low"); else escalation_tier ("insufficient_evidence" when noninferior is None or n < min_samples, else "soft_escalation"); a chosen tier that is unavailable falls back to the other available tier for soft decisions (append "fallback:<tier>_unavailable"); none available -> hold, hold_reason "no_planner_tier_available".
- record(decision, *, subject, route, jev_signal=None, root=None) -> decision_log.record(kind="planner_route", subject=goal id, candidates=list(decision.candidates), hard_constraints=list(decision.hard_reasons), deterministic={"route": route name, "reason": route reason}, historical=dict(decision.evidence), jev=jev_signal, selected="hold" if decision.hold else decision.tier, rejected=[c for c in candidates if c != selected], reason=";".join(decision.reasons), mode=decision.mode, extra={"decision_type": decision.decision_type, "hold_reason": decision.hold_reason, "shadow_tier": decision.shadow_tier, "soft_score": decision.soft_score}, root=root).
- explain(decision) -> one line. decision_log.py change: append "planner_route" to KINDS only.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_router.py::test_mode_off_reproduces_route_tier — mode off returns the route tier (fable) with reasons ('mode_off',), shadow_tier None, hold False for every decision type; a non-escalate route returns its own tier unchanged in every mode; candidates is always (opus, fable)

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_hard_escalation_never_downgrades_and_holds_when_fable_unavailable — complexity 9, security, ambiguous_requirement and repeated_spec_rejection each yield tier fable, hard True and reasons == hard_reasons in active mode even with noninferior evidence and jev soft_adjust -0.2; with fable unavailable the decision is hold True with hold_reason starting fable_unavailable; a ctx without complexity and band 7-10 does not hard-escalate on complexity

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_shadow_mode_keeps_fable_and_sets_shadow_tier — shadow mode yields tier fable and shadow_tier opus for a soft decision, shadow_tier None for a hard decision, when opus is unavailable, or when sample exceeds shadow_sample_rate

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_active_mode_requires_evidence_and_ignores_tokens — active with n 25 noninferior True picks opus; n 5 picks fable with reason insufficient_evidence; noninferior False picks fable; evidence carrying tokens_saved 1e9 changes nothing; fable_reserve_ok False with noninferior None picks opus with reason fable_reserve_low; fable_reserve_ok(0.1, cfg) is False and fable_reserve_ok(None, cfg) is True

tests/test_planner_router.py::test_load_cfg_defaults_and_record_kind — missing table gives every documented default; an invalid mode falls back to shadow with exactly one notify.notify call across two load_cfg calls and no bus access; record(decision, subject, route, jev_signal) appends a decision_log row of kind planner_route whose candidates, rejected, deterministic.route, jev and extra.decision_type are set, readable by decision_log.explain under a sandbox root

constraints.interface_contract: load_cfg(pool_cfg) -> dict is the single reader of [planner.routing]: mode shadow|off|active (default shadow), default_tier opus, escalation_tier fable, hard_complexity_min 9, hard_security true, hard_spec_review_request_changes_min 2, hard_ambiguous true, min_samples 20, shadow_sample_rate 1.0, fable_reserve_share 0.2, jev_mode shadow, soft_threshold 0.5. fable_reserve_ok(headroom_share, cfg) -> bool. effective_complexity(classification, ctx) -> int via BAND_FLOOR. RouterDecision(tier, mode, hard, hold, hold_reason, reasons, hard_reasons, soft_score, shadow_tier, candidates=(default, escalation), evidence, decision_type). decide(classification, ctx, route, *, cfg, availability, evidence, jev_signal=None, sample=1.0) -> RouterDecision; all structured inputs are dicts. record(decision, *, subject, route, jev_signal=None, root=None) writes decision_log kind planner_route. Tiers are aliases resolved by the caller: fable -> [models].planner, opus -> [models].opus.

result.summary:
Implemented Planner routing modes, hard escalation holds, evidence gates, reserve handling, and decision logging.
Gate: passed, 952 tests; working tree clean.
Commit: `4d4f30a1959740f29c033180f5be5567ee752e73`

Files changed:
- `orchestrator/planner_router.py`: +209
- `orchestrator/decision_log.py`: +1
- `tests/test_planner_router.py`: +194

Failures-only test output: empty.

spec_review_risks.issue: decide() rule 1 sets tier = route.tier or "fable" for any non-escalate route. decision.route() only sets tier for "investigate" (sonnet) and "escalate" (fable); "routine" and "none" routes get tier=None, so this line silently defaults them to fable. Currently harmless because planner_runs.tick() (line 1360) filters out routine/none before any router call, but that filtering lives in a file this task cannot touch and a future Wave B wiring mistake would route free/cheap decisions to the expensive tier without any test in this module catching it.

BAND_FLOOR fallback of 0 for an unrecognized/None band means effective_complexity is 0 whenever both ctx["complexity"] is absent and classification["band"] is None (attribution.band returns None for complexity=None). That silently disables the complexity hard-escalation path rather than failing closed, but it is explicitly covered by acceptance criterion 2 ("a ctx without complexity and band 7-10 does not hard-escalate"), so this is a documented design choice, not an oversight — flagging only so the reviewer of the merged diff confirms the fail-open default here is intentional given decision.py fails closed elsewhere (unknown ctx fields -> escalate).
